result:
Done. I tested `pypdf._reader` (specifically `PdfReader`) with property-based tests covering valid parsing, writer→reader round-trips, bounded-time behavior on malformed trailers, and byte-level corruption fuzzing.

**2 passing properties**: valid PDFs parse with correct page geometry; `PdfWriter`→`PdfReader` round-trips preserve page sizes and metadata.

**2 genuine bugs found**, both in `PdfReader.root_object`:

1. **`bug_report_pypdf__reader_2026-10-06_01-50_ff72.md` (Medium, Logic)** — When the trailer has no valid `/Root`, the fallback search loops over `range(trailer["/Size"])`, and `/Size` is untrusted. Each missing object triggers a full-file regex scan, so runtime is O(`/Size` × file length). A 222-byte file with `/Size 100000` takes 2.5 s; a 1 MB file with `/Size 2000` takes 34 s. Fix: iterate only over object numbers actually present in the parsed xref/object-stream maps.

2. **`bug_report_pypdf__reader_2026-10-06_01-52_10uv.md` (Medium, Crash)** — When `/Root` resolves to a non-dictionary object (e.g. a `NumberObject`), `root_object` calls `.get("/Type")` on it and raises a bare `AttributeError` instead of a `PdfReadError`, bypassing callers' `except PyPdfError` handlers. The sibling `_info` property already guards against this; `root_object` does not. Fix: add `isinstance(..., DictionaryObject)` guards (confirmed the naive one-line fix just shifts the crash to a later `/Pages` check, so the patch guards both sites).

Both are reproduced with standalone scripts using correctly-structured PDFs, so they represent realistic malformed-file handling rather than contrived edge cases.
